subject: Post-call: pricing & token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom@acmeailabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + pricing benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Tom — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our call so your finance and infra teams have what they need. Thanks again for sharing the high-level usage patterns.

Recap (as discussed)
- Workload: multi-turn retrieval + generation for customer support automation.
- Expected steady-state token profile: 150M–300M tokens/month initially, potential to scale to 1B+ over 12–18 months if pilot metrics look good.
- SLA/latency needs: P50 < 250ms for short responses; some A/B traffic can tolerate higher latency.

Pricing & unit economics we discussed (ballpark)
- Target from Acme: $/1M tokens target in the $50–$100 range depending on commit.
- Host benchmarking (examples we referenced):
  * OpenAI (hosted Davinci-like): ~$120/1M tokens (generation + prompt combined, illustrative).
  * Anthropic (Claude-style hosted): ~$140/1M tokens (higher for long context + higher-quality generation).
  * Open-model hosts (self-hosted or managed): ranges widely; typical committed pricing we see ~$40–$90/1M depending on model variant, quantization, and reserved capacity.

How Redwood can help (pricing levers)
- Hosted API: simple REST/SDK with volume tiers and optional committed discounts; good for getting started quickly.
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity: predictable $/1M at lower tiers for larger commits (we can get into the $30s–$60s/1M for sizeable multi-month commits and model quantization).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise pricing with commitment and support — best for regulated customers where unit economics and data isolation both matter.

Immediate next steps
1) I’ll send a concise pricing benchmarking sheet (attached) showing example $/1M math at 150M, 500M, and 1B tokens vs OpenAI/Anthropic and a couple of open-model hosts. (Attached: token-benchmarks-1M.csv, redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx)
2) If the numbers look promising, propose a 6–8 week pilot on Redwood Hosted with a 3-month committed reservation option to lock a lower $/1M.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya to validate request profiles and any JNI/SDK integration questions.

Let us know what exact $/1M target your procurement would need for an internal approval (we can model a couple of commit scenarios). I’ll follow up with the benchmarking attachment in a separate email thread within the hour.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx (pricing table, commit tiers)
Attachment: token-benchmarks-1M.csv (example cost math)
From: Tom Reed <tom@acmeailabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Vanessa — thanks for the recap and fast follow. Helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Expected steady-state for budgeting: probably ~200M tokens/month for Q2, trending to ~500M if we move forward by Q4.
- Procurement target: our finance PM asked for target $/1M in the $50–$75 range to be viable for internal approval. We can stretch to $100/1M if there are strong SLA and support guarantees.
- Comparison ask: finance wants three line-item comparisons (OpenAI, Anthropic, Redwood committed / Redwood hosted) for 200M and 500M volumes — show monthly $ cost and per-token effective $/1M after discounts.

Can you also confirm whether the dedicated reserved capacity pricing you mentioned assumes model quantization (e.g., int8) or matches float32 performance? Performance/quality tradeoffs matter to our product folks.

If you can get those numbers over today, I’ll share with procurement and book time for a security questionnaire review next week.

—Tom
Tom Reed
Head of Product Ops | Acme AI Labs
tom@acmeailabs.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom@acmeailabs.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Tom — looping in Aditya for the technical side, and adding the quick benchmark table here (summary) before Vanessa sends the full sheet: 

Summary bench (illustrative) — cost per month
- 200M tokens:
  * OpenAI: ~$24,000 (implied $120/1M)
  * Anthropic: ~$28,000 (implied $140/1M)
  * Redwood Hosted (no commit): ~$16,000–$20,000 (implied $80–$100/1M)
  * Redwood Dedicated (6 mo commit, quantized models): ~$6,000–$12,000 (implied $30–$60/1M depending on model variant + batch/kv cache)
- 500M tokens:
  * OpenAI: ~$60,000 (implied $120/1M)
  * Anthropic: ~$70,000 (implied $140/1M)
  * Redwood Hosted (no commit): ~$40,000–$50,000 (implied $80–$100/1M)
  * Redwood Dedicated (6 mo commit, quantized): ~$15,000–$30,000 (implied $30–$60/1M)

Notes:
- Dedicated pricing assumes use of quantized model variants we support (int8 or similar) and a committed reserved capacity profile; exact numbers vary by model mix and latency SLOs.
- Hosted no-commit pricing is higher but includes zero infra ops and immediate availability.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Vanessa to send the attached spreadsheet with exact line-item math for 200M and 500M scenarios (we’ll include both hosted and dedicated options and an optional 6-month commit).
2) Aditya to run a quick perf/quality note: we’ll highlight model choices (float vs int8) and expected latency differentials so you can evaluate the quality tradeoffs.

Vanessa — can you attach the benchmarking CSV and follow-up with a proposed pilot term (6–8 weeks) and the committed pricing tiers?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Tom — attaching the benchmarking file and the Redwood pricing sheet as promised. Quick highlights inline: 

- For your goal of $50–$75/1M: our Hosted plan without commit sits above that range for 200M (roughly $80–$100/1M).
- With a 6-month reserved capacity commitment and using our quantized model profiles we can get into the $30–$55/1M band depending on model mix and latency SLOs (this is the Dedicated pricing shown in the attachment).
- I’ve included two commit scenarios in the spreadsheet: 6 months and 12 months, plus an example pilot add-on (8-week pilot with a small committed minimum to prove latency and quality).

Next items: 
- I’ll set up a 30-min tech validation with Aditya for Monday 2/16 at 10am PT (invite sent).
- If procurement wants a formal quote, let me know which commit tier (6mo vs 12mo) and target model family; we’ll prepare a signed quote for review.

Appreciate the clarity on the $50–$75 target — I included a modeling tab so you can see the math at 200M and 500M tokens.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
